question: According to representatives of the agricultural associations of Eastern Macedonia, the extreme temperatures and prolonged drought of 2024 caused significant losses in maize production, putting many producers at risk of not meeting the minimum production thresholds required to receive coupled aid. They argue that the loss of production is solely due to extreme weather events and not the fault of farmers.

Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 provides Member States with flexibility in the implementation of direct payments, while Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 recognises the concept of force majeure and exceptional circumstances. Maintaining agricultural production and producers’ income is critical for food security and the viability of rural areas. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Does it consider that Member States have sufficient flexibility to derogate from the minimum production thresholds for the granting of coupled payments in cases of proven extreme weather events?
Does it intend to issue additional guidelines for the uniform application of the concept of force majeure in the context of the CAP?
Does it intend to consider further flexibilities under the CAP to ensure that coupled payments are maintained in areas systematically affected by adverse weather conditions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.10.2026) Member States may recognise severe meteorological events as force majeure where abnormal and unforeseeable circumstances beyond the beneficiary’s control, despite the exercise of all due care, prevent compliance with the relevant Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) requirements – whether stemming from EU regulations or specific national conditions.

This is thus also applicable to coupled income support (CIS). The recognition of cases of force majeure is to be decided by the competent national authority, normally on a case-by-case basis. Where an event gravely affects a well-determined area, EU law1 allows the Member State to consider the whole area gravely affected. Force majeure does not, as such, modify or derogate from applicable requirements.

However, under Article 59(5) of the same Regulation, where non-compliance is due to force majeure or exceptional circumstances, no penalty is imposed and the beneficiary retains the right to receive the aid. The Commission Communication COM(2024) 2252 provides comprehensive clarification on the application of force majeure under the CAP. Additional guidelines are therefore not needed.

The current rules give the Member States flexibility in designing CIS interventions to address sectors or specific types of farming that are facing structural difficulties and are important for socio-economic or environmental reasons, with support conditions adapted to national, regional or local needs. This approach is maintained in the proposal for the CAP post-2027.

It would allow Member States to adjust or propose new support options, where needed, to adapt to evolving needs on the ground, but CIS is not a tool to address income losses due to (recurring) crisis events.
1 Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) 2021/2116. 2 Communication from the Commission to the Council on force majeure and exceptional circumstances in
